newsitem.title: USA: CIBA Vision to pay $5 million in settlement.
newsitem.headline: CIBA Vision to pay $5 million in settlement.

text.p: Ciba Vision Inc. has agreed to pay $5 million in a 25-state settlement for its alleged involvement in a scheme to keep replacement contact lenses out of the hands of retailers and under the control of more expensive sources, including optometrists, the state attorney general said Monday.
Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger said in a statement that the settlement still has to be approved by a federal judge in Jacksonville, Fla.
Ciba Vision is owned by Novartis AG.

In class action and state lawsuits, the Mass. Attorney General's office and others alleged that Ciba Vision, along with Johnson & Johnson's Vistakon, Bausch & Lomb Inc., the American Optometric Association and other defendants conspired not to sell replacement contact lenses directly to retailers such as pharmacies and mail-order companies.
Similar class action suits have been filed in 24 states.
Lens makers and eye care professionals may have overcharged consumers by $600 million between 1989 and 1994, according to a spokesman for New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco.

The optometrists are accused of pressuring manufacturers to limit consumer access to soft contact lens prescriptions, which are necessary in order for consumers to purchase from lower-priced outlets such as mail-order companies and pharmacies.
Ciba Vision, which did not admit any wrongdoing, has agreed to give consumers up to $43 in rebates and free products, the Mass. Attorney General's office said.
The settlement does not end the lawsuits pending against Vistakon, Bausch & Lomb, eight optometric associations and 11 optometrists.

Ciba has changed its distribution policy to make its contact lenses available thorugh mail-order, pharmacies and other ways, and, according to the settlement, the policy must be in place for five years.
Other manufacturers have not changed their policy, the Mass. Attorney General's office said.
